questions.stem: Why do addition reactions have higher atom economy than substitution reactions?

options.text: Addition reactions use more expensive reagents
In addition reactions, all atoms from the reactants end up in the product with no by-products

questions.explanation: Addition reactions have 100% atom economy because all atoms from the reactants are incorporated into a single product with no by-products. For example, C2H4 + H2O -> C2H5OH uses all atoms. Substitution reactions produce by-products (e.g., C2H5Br + NaOH -> C2H5OH + NaBr has only 31% atom economy).
